reason: No feature drawn on the plan can be identified on the imagery: the fortifications, excavated structures and moat are buried or backfilled, the unfarmed mound is bounded by straight field edges rather than by any drawn contour, and the plan shows no road, track, village, well or survey mark. No auxiliary plan with surviving features is available.

candidates_considered.feature: Indus fortification of the lower town and acropolis (confirmed, conjectured and suspected lines, with bastions)
candidates_considered.why: buried; the drawn circuit (about 380 m by 320 m) is larger than the unfarmed mound (about 245 m by 265 m), and its west, north and east lines fall in cultivated fields with no trace in any release

candidates_considered.feature: Harappan defence wall of the acropolis (thick black, about 200 m long, curving from north-west to south)
candidates_considered.why: no linear masonry, trench or spoil line can be seen inside the protected area at 0.52 m per pixel in any of the seven images; the straight eastern stretch of the modern ring track is the only long line there, and nothing ties it to the wall

candidates_considered.feature: moat and east fortification with steps, drain-cum-tie-wall and entrance
candidates_considered.why: the strip east of the ring track is unfarmed but shows only trees, a guard hut and bare ground; no moat depression or wall line is visible

candidates_considered.feature: excavated structures (houses, well, drains, pre-Harappan structures, south entrance)
candidates_considered.why: the trenches are backfilled or overgrown; one rectangular outline about 18 m by 23 m in the north-west of the mound (release 8432, near mosaic px 885-920, 915-960) cannot be matched to any one drawn structure

candidates_considered.feature: contours (209-216 m) and the mound outline
candidates_considered.why: the unfarmed area is bounded on the north, west and east by straight field edges of the cadastral grid, not by a landform, and the drawn mound extends well beyond it; no contour corner or re-entrant can be identified on the imagery

candidates_considered.feature: dry bed of the Sarasvati (stippled band at the south-west of the plan)
candidates_considered.why: drawn schematically, about 200 m south of the town by the plan's own note; no channel edge is visible in the fields south of the mound

candidates_considered.feature: modern features (protected-area fence, ring tracks, guard hut, small platform, village of Banawali to the north-east)
candidates_considered.why: none of these is drawn on the plan

candidates_considered.feature: auxiliary plan through which to chain the registration
candidates_considered.why: the other figures of the IAR 1987-88 entry (PDF page indices 31 and 33) are sections; no Banawali plan with surviving modern features was found in the publications in plan-B/downloads

notes: The site was found at the published coordinates: an unfarmed, fenced mound about 245 m east-west by 265 m north-south among fields, 1 km south-west of Banawali village, with a ring track, a guard hut on its east side and a small platform near its centre. Zoom 19 is not available. We examined the current image (Vantor Vivid, 20230508) and Wayback releases 8432, 16749, 47471, 64776, 20337 and 52304 at zoom 18; none shows excavation trenches, wall lines or a moat. While checking which pages of the IAR 1983-84 PDF were figures we printed the first 200 characters of each page; on PDF page index 33 this showed a sentence stating that the wall exposed in Tr OC runs roughly NW-SE and represents the north-eastern arm of the fortification. We read no further text of the Banawali entry.
